traceability.evidence: Rule implementation: src/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.ts defines the ESLint rule `prefer-implements-annotation` that detects legacy `@story` + `@req` usage, detects mixed/multi-story patterns, and provides a conservative auto-fix: - JSDoc header explicitly maps to this story and requirements: - `@story docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md` - `@req REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING`, `REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT`, `REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX`, `REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT`, `REQ-VALID-OUTPUT`, `REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION`, `REQ-AUTO-FIX`. - `analyzeComment` and `processComment` implement legacy detection and messages (REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING, REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT): - If a block has both `@story` and `@req` and no `@supports`, it reports `messageId: 'preferImplements'` (optional recommendation warning). - If it mixes `@story`/`@req` with `@supports`, it reports `messageId: 'cannotAutoFix'` with `reason: "comment mixes @story/@req with existing @supports annotations"`. - If it finds more than one distinct `@story` path (multi-story), it reports `messageId: 'multiStoryDetected'`. - Auto-fix implementation (REQ-AUTO-FIX, REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX, REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT, REQ-VALID-OUTPUT): - `collectStoryAndReqMetadata` parses the block comment, collecting: - `storyLineIndices`, `reqLineIndices`, `reqIds`, and `storyPath` for simple `@story`/`@req` lines only. - It explicitly bails out (`storyPath = null`) when `@story` or `@req` lines have extra tokens (complex descriptions), ensuring no fix is produced for ambiguous patterns. - `buildImplementsAutoFix` only returns a fixer when: - `storyPaths.size === 1` (single story), - exactly one `@story` line (`storyLineIndices.length === 1`), - at least one `@req` line (`reqLineIndices.length >= 1`), and - `storyPath !== null` (simple forms only). In that case it builds a fixer that will: - Remove the original `@story` and all `@req` lines. - Replace the `@story` line with a single `@supports ...` line using the same leading prefix. - `applyImplementsReplacement` preserves comment structure and ordering: - It derives `linePrefix` from the original `@story` line via `const prefixMatch = storyRawLine.match(/^(\s*\*?\s*)/)` and reuses it for the new `@supports` line. - It iterates `rawLines`, replacing only the `storyIdx` line with the new `@supports` line and skipping only the `@story`/`@req` lines in `allIndicesToRemove`. All other lines (e.g., description or `@param`) are preserved in place, ensuring the new annotation stays in the same relative position within the JSDoc block (REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT).,Rule metadata and configuration behavior (REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING, REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY, REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION): - In src/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.ts, `meta` is defined as: - `type: 'suggestion'` and `docs.recommended: false` – this rule is explicitly a recommendation-only migration aid, not part of the recommended preset. - `fixable: 'code'` – ESLint auto-fix support is declared. - `messages` exactly match the story's recommended messages: - `preferImplements: "Consider using @supports instead of @story + @req for clearer traceability. Run ESLint with --fix to auto-convert."` - `cannotAutoFix: "Cannot auto-fix: {{reason}}. Manual migration to @supports required."` - `multiStoryDetected: "Multiple @story annotations detected in the same comment block. Manually convert to separate @supports lines."` - `schema: []` – no custom options; severity is controlled solely via ESLint rule severity (`off` / `warn` / `error`), satisfying the "configurable enforcement" requirement. - In src/index.ts: - The plugin’s `RULE_NAMES` array includes `"prefer-implements-annotation"`, ensuring the rule is exported and available to consumers. - The `TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES` map (used to build `configs.recommended` and `configs.strict`) does NOT include `traceability/prefer-implements-annotation`, so the built-in flat configs do not enable this rule at any severity. - `configs.recommended` and `configs.strict` are created solely from `TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES`, confirming the new rule is disabled by default and legacy validation behavior remains unchanged unless the user opts in (REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY, REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION).,Targeted unit tests for this story: tests/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.test.ts - File header ties tests directly to this story and its key requirements: - `Tests for: docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md` - `@story docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md` - `@req` tags for `REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING`, `REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT`, and `REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY`. - Behavior tests for core rule logic and backward compatibility (REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING, REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT, REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION): - `valid` cases: - "[REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION] comment with only @story is ignored" – confirms the rule does not report when only `@story` is present. - "[REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION] comment with only @req is ignored" – confirms only `@req` also produces no diagnostics. - "[REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION] comment with @supports only is ignored" – the modern form is not redundantly reported, verifying both formats remain valid when the recommendation rule is present. - `invalid` cases: - "[REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING] single-story @story + @req block triggers preferImplements message" – ensures detection of the legacy pattern with `messageId: 'preferImplements'`. - "[REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT] mixed @story/@req and @supports triggers cannotAutoFix" – verifies the `cannotAutoFix` message and its `reason` data when `@supports` is already present. - Expected `output`: ```js /** * @supports docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED */ function autoFixSingleReq() {} ``` - This verifies that the rule’s auto-fix converts simple `@story` + `@req` into a single `@supports` line as specified. - Single-story, multiple-requirement auto-fix (REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX): - Test: "[REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX] single @story with multiple @req lines auto-fixes to single @supports line containing all REQ IDs". - Confirms that all `@req` IDs are preserved in order and merged into one `@supports` line. - Safety for complex/ambiguous patterns (REQ-VALID-OUTPUT): - "[REQ-AUTO-FIX] complex @req content (extra description) does not auto-fix but still warns" – complex `@req` line (with extra text) triggers `preferImplements` but **no `output`** is specified, so RuleTester asserts the code is unchanged (warning only, no fix). - `describe("prefer-implements-annotation configuration severity (REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY)", ...)` contains two tests: - Verifies the rule is **not** enabled by default in either `configs.recommended` or `configs.strict`: - Together with src/index.ts, this confirms the rule is opt-in, controlled entirely via standard ESLint severity configuration, and disabled by default for backward compatibility.,Documentation for the rule and migration workflow (REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING, REQ-AUTO-FIX, REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY, documentation AC): - traceability.notes: The story 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS is fully implemented. The `prefer-implements-annotation` rule exists and is wired into the plugin, is disabled by default, and can be enabled with standard ESLint severities. It detects legacy `@story` + `@req` annotations and emits configurable recommendations; detects mixed and multi-story patterns and reports them as non-auto-fixable; and provides a conservative auto-fix that converts single-story `@story` + multiple `@req` lines into a single `@supports` line while preserving JSDoc structure and formatting. Tests explicitly cover optional warnings, auto-fix behavior (including single- and multi-`@req` cases), non-fixable edge cases, backward compatibility (ignoring comments that only contain `@story`, `@req`, or `@supports`), and configuration defaults. Documentation includes both internal rule details and a user-facing migration guide describing opt-in configuration and the nature of the auto-fixes. All related tests pass in the full suite. The only minor discrepancy is that docs/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.md references a slightly different story filename in its `@story` tag, but this does not affect behavior and does not invalidate any acceptance criteria. Overall, every acceptance criterion and listed requirement for this story has concrete implementation and test evidence, so the story is assessed as PASSED.
